apps.name: Terra Incognita
apps.subtitle: The world, and the toys on it
apps.localizedDescription: The whole Earth as satellites saw it this month, and on it a living light for each of the toys, each where its thing really happens: starlings in Somerset, fireflies in the Smokies, the swell at Nazaré, a river on the Beni, frost on a window at Oymyakon. Touch one and fall into it. Offline; every dataset credited.

apps.subtitle: Your finger is warm
apps.localizedDescription: A cabin window at Oymyakon, about −50 °C, the night outside. Frost creeps in from the frame, each crystal at its own angle, meeting its neighbours along seams. Your finger is warm: what you wipe stays clear, the frost creeping back only slowly from its edges. Real snow-crystal physics (Reiter's model). A toy; offline.

apps.subtitle: Lightning over Lake Maracaibo; your finger is the ground
apps.localizedDescription: Night over Lake Maracaibo, where the Catatumbo meets it and lightning flickers most nights of the year. Touch the water and a stroke forks down to your finger, grown by the rule real lightning follows; hold and it strikes again down the same channel. Every piece of the channel thunders, the near ones first. Touch the sky for a crawler under the cloud. Working title; a toy in the making.

apps.name: Moon Road
apps.subtitle: The moon paints its road down Lake Superior
apps.localizedDescription: Moonrise over Lake Superior, the water a numbered template on dark paper. Only the bits of water tilted just right send the moon's light to your eye, and each one the moon lights, it paints, so the road of light from the moon to you fills in, number by number. Tap for a gust and the road spreads; drag to walk the shore and the road follows you. Shake for a fresh page. Working title; a toy in the making.

apps.subtitle: Sand-bubbler crabs drawing starbursts at low tide
apps.localizedDescription: Low tide on a Phuket beach, seen from above. Sand-bubbler crabs feed out from their burrows and leave the sifted sand behind as little balls, laid in spokes, and the beach fills with starbursts nobody drew. Tap for a footstep and they bolt, their neighbours after them; drag to draw in the sand; shake and the tide comes in. Working title; a toy in the making.

apps.name: Barchans
apps.subtitle: Crescent dunes walking the Sahara; drag to turn the wind
apps.localizedDescription: Dunes near Tarfaya in the Atlantic Sahara, from above in a low sun. One rule (the wind lifts sand, drops it downwind, and it sticks best on sand) makes crescents that walk, merge and calve. Drag to turn the wind and watch them turn; hold still to pour sand. A big dune's sliding face hums at a hundred hertz. Working title; a toy in the making.

apps.subtitle: One aspen that looks like a forest, from the grove to a leaf's pores
apps.localizedDescription: Pando, in Utah, looks like a forest of golden aspens but is one tree: over 40,000 stems from one root. Drag to blow and gusts run over the grove as pale waves, every leaf flipping on its flat stalk. Tap a tree, then a leaf, then closer still, to its pores, which close in your finger's shade. Working title; a toy in the making.

apps.name: Hoh
apps.subtitle: The rainforest below Mount Olympus, where fallen logs grow rows of trees
apps.localizedDescription: The Hoh, at the foot of Mount Olympus in Washington. Moss smothers every seedling on the forest floor; only those on a fallen log live, so young trees grow in lines along the logs, and when a log rots away its trees stand in a row on stilts. Drag to run the years; tap a giant to fell it. Working title; a toy in the making.
